admitted.text: She reads as long underfed in every sense, so that plain kindness bowls her over.
admitted.detail_quote: This is the nicest a person has been to me in a really long time. And it's froyo.

admitted.text: She seems to carry her mother's shame about her body into every moment she is looked at.
admitted.detail_quote: She had spent since she was fourteen hiding it under long coats and loose things, keeping it folded small.

admitted.text: She seems to explain away whatever she feels for Randi before she can look at it.
admitted.detail_quote: She'd hardly slept. She was still so full of him, of the whole weekend. She put it down to that.

admitted.text: She reads as wholly trusting and unsuspecting, convinced that the two most important people in her life met her by pure chance and barely know each other.
admitted.detail_quote: It had come to her all of a piece, the one and then the other, in six weeks, for no reason she had done anything to deserve.

admitted.text: She seems to need a name for what she and Pace are, and refuses to be paid in deeds alone.
admitted.detail_quote: She had said her best sentence. He had not said the sentence back.

admitted.text: She reads as a loyal, tactful friend who protects other people's shame.
admitted.detail_quote: the kindest thing a friend could do was not make her carry it in front of anyone.

admitted.text: Vee seems most alive when choosing exposure for herself, turning the body she once hid into an instrument of daring.
admitted.detail_quote: Not the kind of woman who is kept for a man's pleasure. The kind a man keeps *in* pleasure.

admitted.text: He reads as truly attentive, someone who sees what she needs and not only what she says.
admitted.detail_quote: and she understood in the space of a breath that he hadn't matched the dress she'd described.

admitted.text: He seems sincerely bound by consent, even while he runs a hidden design.
admitted.detail_quote: She chooses it, Randi. Every step of it. Or it isn't anything.

admitted.text: He is unsettling, because the courtship began as a private erotic game for two.
admitted.detail_quote: He had no name for the game yet, only the live private charge of something he imagined they could make together.

admitted.text: He reads as a man who holds back the word "love" out of fear, not coldness.
admitted.detail_quote: He had hurt her because he was afraid of how much she could hurt him.

admitted.text: He reads as deeply isolated under all his social ease.
admitted.detail_quote: You make a friend from the middle of the pack — you lose to him, and lose again, and come out the other side friends. I was never once in the pack.

admitted.text: He seems not to see that the Daphne arrangement was exploitative.
admitted.detail_quote: Which was its own joke — there was nothing in the catalog I needed tutoring in.

admitted.text: She seems to have been both Pace's whole world and the wound he still misnames as luck.
admitted.detail_quote: Not with her. It was the best two years I'd had. And then it was over.

admitted.text: She reads as someone who lives behind a practiced face and has decided never to come out from behind it.
admitted.detail_quote: The one he had found was going back behind it, and she was not coming out again.

admitted.text: She reads as a woman who uses immaculate beauty and social poise as armor so that no one can ever reach or hurt her real self.
admitted.detail_quote: The face took the being-looked-at, the being-wanted, the being-touched, and none of it reached any further than the face, because the face was not her.

admitted.text: Her eating seems tightly policed, a hunger she keeps rationed.
admitted.detail_quote: He watched the thing behind her face that policed her relationship to food run through whatever calculation it was running

admitted.text: She reads as manipulative, drawing out Vee's confessions and then pulling back at the peak.
admitted.detail_quote: It was gentle. It was kind. It was a door closing softly.

admitted.text: She seems to be in love with Vee and too frightened to say so.
admitted.detail_quote: Vee was the best friend she had ever had. She loved Vee and she had told her so, more than once.

admitted.text: Her desire for Vee seems to be slipping past the cover story that it is "for us."
admitted.detail_quote: She had made herself not a woman who hungered for another woman, which he could see was unsurvivable, but a girlfriend offering her man a gift, which was merely sexy.

admitted.text: She seems resentful of Pace's unhurried hold on Vee.
admitted.detail_quote: Her hands were flat on the cloth on either side of the bowl she had not eaten from

admitted.text: He reads as the faultless, safe life that leaves Randi untouched.
admitted.detail_quote: This man had taken a beautiful woman to bed, brought her pleasure, but never found her underneath.

admitted.text: She reads as coldly punitive, someone who shames by quiet display rather than words.
admitted.detail_quote: They're not mine. They're your color.

admitted.text: She reads as fiercely and privately loyal to Vee.
admitted.detail_quote: The whole forty seconds Vee had spent being a student, Cassie had spent watching what the dress had done to her friend, because the friend was the only part of any of it Cassie had ever been able to see.

admitted.text: Cassie seems protective without trying to own Vee, repeatedly allowing silences and pivots that other people would pry open.
admitted.detail_quote: Cassie let the pivot happen. She was good at that.

admitted.text: She reads as the one person who will tell Pace the hard truth.
admitted.detail_quote: She didn't want him, she wasn't impressed by him, and she'd say so to his face; she just liked him and gave him hell.

admitted.text: She seems warm on the surface and calculating underneath, the house's watchful enforcer.
admitted.detail_quote: She ran a house of ninety and she knew to the inch what every room in it was worth.

admitted.text: She reads as steady and unflappable.
admitted.detail_quote: Meg was the calm one, dark-haired and level, a girl who ate like she had all night

admitted.text: She reads as warm, nonstop exuberance.
admitted.detail_quote: Don't do anything I wouldn't do

admitted.text: He seems a gracious, slightly wistful friend who took rejection well.
admitted.detail_quote: He took it like a gentleman. He's nice.

admitted.text: Vee's mother reads as loving yet invasive, her concern inseparable from the shame and bodily policing she has taught her daughter.
admitted.detail_quote: the second voice came, the one that lived in her mother's mouth and had moved into hers

admitted.text: The bench: a built thing that waits, standing for the design Pace keeps hidden in plain sight.
admitted.detail_quote: full of what it was, doing what it would continue to do, waiting for the next time.

admitted.text: The thin apple slices: Randi's rationed appetite, and Pace's wish to feed it.
admitted.detail_quote: a girl who had been portioning herself, weighing every want before she let herself have it

admitted.text: The cap pressed under her thumbnail: a private self-punishment Randi repeats with glass rims.
admitted.detail_quote: She kept the bottle when she was done, turning the cap loose in her fingers, and set the sharp inner edge of the cap under her thumbnail and pressed — slow and steady, down into the nail bed, where it would hurt.

admitted.text: The deadbolt: Randi locking her true self away for good.
admitted.detail_quote: she always locked it behind her, first thing, before anything else

admitted.text: Randi's white-gold bracelet: the one fixed, locked thing under all her changing surfaces.
admitted.detail_quote: Randi felt her own bracelet, plain white gold, locked on her wrist, and kept it out of the light.

admitted.text: The burgundy dress: Pace's love, given as care with the effort hidden.
admitted.detail_quote: that he'd taken all that trouble and then taken the further trouble to hide the trouble

admitted.text: The flannel shirt: a stand-in for Pace that cannot give her the word she wants.
admitted.detail_quote: And it was warm because she was warm. That was the thing she couldn't stop feeling once she'd felt it — the heat in the shirt was her own, given back.

admitted.text: Vee's green panties in Randi's fist: Vee held between the lovers without knowing it.
admitted.detail_quote: the spot exactly where she'd put it

admitted.text: The pastry glaze on Vee's lip: Randi's touch left on her, unnoticed.
admitted.detail_quote: there was a thread of sweetness, sugar and butter and something warm under it, the glaze of a pastry she had never once touched.

admitted.text: The emptied bathroom drawer: Pace speaking only through deeds.
admitted.detail_quote: He hadn't told her it didn't matter. He'd gone and made her a place instead.

admitted.text: the outlier: hidden family corruption that becomes visible only when personal data interrupts a clean general story
admitted.detail_quote: the biggest one, off on its own in the white

admitted.text: The stained coat lining: proof of Vee's wanting that she now owns rather than hides.
admitted.detail_quote: the dark bloom of herself she'd never be able to explain to a soul

admitted.text: Mauss's gift: gifts that bind, like the dress, the shoes and the meals.
admitted.detail_quote: A gift carries what they called *hau* — the spirit of the one who gave it.

admitted.text: waxing bare: desire as willing transformation entangled with pain, ignorance, submission, and borrowed expertise
admitted.detail_quote: his hand, the right hand, the one she'd kept everything back for

admitted.text: The unfinished reach to her own fingers: Vee one breath short of accepting her own desire.
admitted.detail_quote: A breath's width remained. She held there until her lungs began to hurt, fingers before her mouth, tongue waiting behind her teeth.

admitted.text: the expensive heels: Randi's lesson that Vee may choose spectacle over apology, shadowed by debt and dependence
admitted.detail_quote: She sat on the edge of the bed and put Randi's heels on, and got the whole of them for the first time with her own feet in them

admitted.text: Will Vee learn that she was chosen in a game Randi and Pace began together?
admitted.detail_quote: Do you think she'll like the bench?

admitted.text: Will Pace ever say he loves Vee?
admitted.detail_quote: Then not saying it matters more to you than having her.

admitted.text: What is the story behind the scar on Pace's thigh?
admitted.detail_quote: He did not take her hand away. He kept it there under his, on the thing he wasn't going to tell her about yet

admitted.text: What did Pace's father do that made home unsafe?
admitted.detail_quote: Went bad with his daddy. He hasn't been home since he was sixteen.

admitted.text: Will Randi give up her place in the sorority or give up Vee?
admitted.detail_quote: You've got a position in this house, and you've got her. You need to choose.

admitted.text: Will Vee ever tell Randi she saw the fraud record?
admitted.detail_quote: the kindest thing a friend could do was not make her carry it in front of anyone

admitted.text: Why did Pace ask Vee to be waxed bare?
admitted.detail_quote: I'd like you waxed," he'd said. "By the weekend. Bare.

admitted.text: Will Randi ever tell Vee plainly, and can she bear what Vee's face would do while she said it?
admitted.detail_quote: That was the one scenario she could not run to the end

admitted.text: What does Vee actually want from Randi — and will she ever let herself know it out loud?
admitted.detail_quote: her body gave one small rock in the seat

admitted.text: How will Vee respond when she discovers Randi minimized or omitted the most painful and exposing parts of the waxing?
admitted.detail_quote: There it was. The part Randi hadn't said.
